findings.F1: The book was in fact always long, whatever the signal: the position after a trade was above 0.01 on 99.9 % of bars (mean allocation 0.93, median 0.87), and its days in a position were 100 %. Its daily returns had a 0.94 correlation with holding the coins, and its deepest fall was -67 % against holding's -81 %. So the failed Calmar (0.38) is the coins' own crashes carried by a near-permanent long, not the idea losing money. Windows w2, w14 and w16 fell -53 %, -55 % and -57 % inside the window.
findings.F2: The effect sits only in the deepest falls. Over 24 hours on the non-overlapping grid, the forecast quintiles 1 to 4 earn an excess of 0.00 %, +0.02 %, +0.02 % and +0.09 % (all t < 0.9, about 1,740 cases each). The top quintile (forecast ≥ 15.7) earns +0.60 % excess (t 4.29, 1,742 cases), and the 1,138 cases at the cap of 20 earn +0.71 % (t 3.84). This is why the idea's size over all 17,241 cases is only +0.01 % unusual move.
findings.F3: For the top quintile, the total move over 24 hours is +0.75 % per case, about 4 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. After that cost it nets +0.56 % per case (t 3.96), with 57.5 % of cases rising.
findings.F4: An approximate book that is long only on top-quintile grid cells and pays 0.19 % per trade had these results: in the market 10 % of the time, a yearly return of +19.4 %, a deepest fall of -21 % (Calmar about 0.92, against 0.75 required) and a Sharpe of 0.86. Holding on the same grid gave +29 % a year with a deepest fall of -76 %.
findings.F5: The rebound keeps building past the idea's horizon. For the top quintile, the excess return is +0.60 % at 24 hours (t 4.28) and +0.78 % at 48 hours (t 4.39); the raw return is +0.42 % at 12 hours, +0.75 % at 24 hours and +1.03 % at 48 hours. Cases at the cap of 20 show +0.71 % and +0.89 % excess (t 3.84 and 3.97).
findings.F6: The deep-fall rebound holds only when the coin's recent volatility is high. Volatility here is the 7-day hourly volatility against the 30-day one, split in thirds.
findings.F7: The deep-fall rebound is on the same side in every coin, with excess from +0.29 % in BTC to +0.84 % in ZEC (t 1.2 to 2.2). It is also there after both 7-day trends (+0.70 % down, t 3.54; +0.46 % up, t 2.40). It is weak in windows w1 to w6 (-0.08 %, t -0.36) and strong in w7 to w18 (+0.98 % and +1.21 %, t 3.5 and 3.2).

ideas.idea: The return over the next 24 hours after a fall over a coin's last 2 hours, at any hour of the day, runs upward, only once the fall is among the coin's deepest 2-hour falls against its usual 2-hour move, and the deeper the fall within those, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader stays out of the coin except after its deepest 2-hour falls, so the book stops carrying the coin's crashes and keeps the rebound that covers a trade's cost several times over.
ideas.name: Only deepest two-hour falls rebound

ideas.idea: The return over the next 48 hours after a fall over a coin's last 2 hours, at any hour of the day, runs upward, and the larger the fall against the coin's usual 2-hour move, the larger the rise, held for two days instead of one.
ideas.consequence: A trader who buys deep 2-hour falls holds them for two days, which captures the larger part of the rebound for the same cost per trade.
ideas.name: Deep fall two-day rebound

ideas.idea: The return over the next 24 hours after a fall over a coin's last 2 hours, at any hour of the day, runs upward, only while the coin's last 7 days have been more volatile than its last 30 days, and the larger the fall against the coin's usual 2-hour move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys deep 2-hour falls only when the coin's recent volatility is raised, and refuses them in calm markets where they do not rebound.
ideas.name: Deep fall rebound, volatile markets
